Q5192081.label: 1948 Cuban general election
Q5192081.summary: General elections were held in Cuba on 1 June 1948. Carlos Prío Socarrás won the presidential election running under the Auténtico-Republican Alliance banner, whilst the Partido Auténtico emerged as the largest party in the House of Representatives, winning 29 of the 70 seats. Voter turnout was 78%.

Q562577.summary: Miguel Ángel Rodríguez Echeverría is a Costa Rican economist, lawyer, businessman and politician who served as the 43rd President of Costa Rica from 1998 to 2002. Q462737.summary: Ahmet Hüsamettin Cindoruk was a Turkish politician and the 17th speaker of the Parliament of Turkey between 1991 and 1995. He was also the acting president of Turkey in 1993 and the leader of two political parties, notably of the True Path Party.

Q583569.label: December murders
Q583569.summary: The December murders were the murders on 7, 8, and 9 December 1982, of fifteen prominent young Surinamese men who had criticized the military dictatorship then ruling Suriname. Thirteen of these men were arrested on December 7 between 2 am and 5 am while sleeping in their homes.

Q851857.label: Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment
Q851857.summary: The Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment is an international human rights treaty under the review of the United Nations that aims to prevent torture and other acts of cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment around the world.

mentions.c: International: Treaty signed: Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment

Q86929.label: 2002 European floods
Q86929.summary: In August 2002, a week of intense rainfall produced flooding across a large portion of Europe. It reached the Ukraine, Italy, Spain, Austria, Germany, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic and Russia. The event killed 232 people and left €27.7 billion (US$27.115 billion) in damage.

Q61732241.label: 2019 Pulwama attack
Q61732241.summary: The 2019 Pulwama attack occurred on 14 February 2019, when a convoy of vehicles carrying Indian security personnel on the Jammu–Srinagar National Highway was attacked by a vehicle-borne suicide bomber at Lethapora in the Pulwama district of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir.

Q709521.label: Battle of Taiyuan
Q709521.desc: 1937 major battle of the Second Sino-Japanese War
Q709521.summary: The Battle of Taiyuan was a major battle fought in 1937 between China and Japan named for Taiyuan, which lay in the 2nd Military Region. The battle concluded in a victory for Japan over the National Revolutionary Army (NRA), including part of Suiyuan, most of Shanxi and the NRA arsenal at Taiyuan, and effectively ended large-scale organized resistance in the North China area.

Q939409.label: Battle of the Litani River
Q939409.img: Australian forces cross the Litani River, 1941.jpg
Q939409.summary: The Battle of the Litani River took place on the advance to Beirut during the Syria-Lebanon campaign of the Second World War. The Australian 7th Division, commanded by Major-General John Lavarack, crossed the Litani River and later clashed with Vichy French troops.

Q4872081.label: Battle of Pork Chop Hill
Q4872081.summary: The Battle of Pork Chop Hill, known as Battle of Seokhyeon-dong Northern Hill in China, is a pair of related Korean War infantry battles that took place on April 16 and July 11, 1953 while the United Nations Command (UN) and the Chinese and North Koreans were negotiating the Korean Armistice Agreement.

Q42886545.label: Operation Geronimo
Q42886545.summary: Operation Geronimo was a joint operation conducted by U.S., South Korean and South Vietnamese forces in Phú Yên Province, lasting from 31 October to 4 December 1966.

Q4727697.label: Alkhan-Yurt massacre
Q4727697.desc: 1999 massacre of Chechen civilians by the Russian Ground Forces
Q4727697.summary: The Alkhan-Yurt massacre was the December 1999 incident in the village of Alkhan-Yurt near the Chechen capital Grozny involving Russian troops under command of General Vladimir Shamanov. The villagers claimed that approximately 41 civilians were killed in the spree, while human rights groups confirmed and documented 17 incidents of murder and three incidents of rape.

mentions.c: Part of Second Chechen War; 17 deaths

Q118151569.label: Battle of Merowe Airport
Q118151569.summary: The battle of Merowe Airport happened in April 2023 during the Sudanese civil war. It involved fighting between the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) for control of the city of Merowe and its airport, and began with the RSF taking over 200 Egyptian soldiers as prisoners of war.

Q127597969.label: July 2024 al-Shati refugee camp attack
Q127597969.desc: military shelling on Gaza City prayer hall
Q127597969.summary: On 13 July 2024, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) conducted an attack against a makeshift mosque in the al-Shati refugee camp in Gaza City. The bombings killed 22 worshippers as they prayed inside the mosque. Palestinian sources reported those killed were civilians, while Israel said it killed "20 Hamas terrorists".

Q16221073.label: Jared Moskowitz
Q16221073.summary: Jared Evan Moskowitz is an American politician and attorney serving as the U.S. representative for Florida's 23rd congressional district since 2023. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously served on the Broward County Commission from 2022 to 2023 and as Director of the Florida Division of Emergency Management from 2019 to 2021. Moskowitz also represented the 97th district in the Florida House of Representatives from 2012 to 2019 and was a city commissioner for Parkland, Florida from 2006 to 2012.

Q611217.label: degrowth
Q611217.desc: economic thinking questioning the benefits and sustainability of economic growth
Q611217.summary: Degrowth is an academic and social movement, predominantly in Europe, aimed at the planned and democratic reduction of production and consumption as a solution to social-ecological crises. Commonly cited policy goals of degrowth include reducing the environmental impact of human activities, redistributing income and wealth within and between countries, and encouraging a shift from materialistic values to a convivial and participatory society.

Q913.label: Socrates
Q913.summary: Socrates was an ancient Greek philosopher from Classical Athens, perhaps the first Western moral philosopher, and a major inspiration on his student Plato, who largely founded the tradition of Western philosophy. An enigmatic figure, Socrates authored no texts and is known mainly through the posthumous accounts of classical writers, particularly his students Plato and Xenophon. These accounts are written as dialogues, in which Socrates and his interlocutors examine a subject in the style of question and answer; they gave rise to the Socratic dialogue literary genre.
